slides.0.title: Industry, Markets and Trade
slides.0.subtitle: Inter Rhône and industry structure
slides.1.title: Industry structure: growers, co-operatives and traders
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Inter Rhône
slides.1.highlights.0.content: The Rhône valley's interprofession, bringing together growers and traders for statistics, promotion and market coordination; most figures here come from its Chiffres clés 2025
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Number of operators
slides.1.highlights.1.content: In 2024/25, 1,418 independent wineries and 87 co-operative wineries sold wine, alongside 366 trading companies; there are also 6,371 production units, professional and non-professional (Inter Rhône, 2025)
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Despatch type
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Cellar despatches in 2024/25 totalled 2,224,791 hl: bulk 64%, packaged 31%, fresh grapes 5%. Most wine moves in bulk to traders who bottle it (Inter Rhône)
slides.1.highlights.3.title: Share of despatches (read from chart)
slides.1.highlights.3.content: The report's chart shows roughly 19% for independent wineries, 18% for co-operatives and 63% for traders. These are chart readings, approximate and not examined
slides.1.content: Essay material: the Rhône's strength is scale through traders and bulk, but it concentrates pricing power with buyers.
slides.2.title: Markets and exports
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Sales and channels
slides.2.highlights.0.content: About 297 million bottles in 2025; roughly two thirds sold in France and one third exported (about 99M bottles by the chart); the channel chart is ambiguous and treated as approximate (Inter Rhône, 2025)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Exports by volume
slides.2.highlights.1.content: 2025 exports: 743,015 hl (-7%) worth €468m (-8%); top five by volume: Belgium 18%, UK 17%, USA 13%, Canada 10%, Germany 8%; China down 36% in volume (Inter Rhône, 2025)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Exports by value
slides.2.highlights.2.content: By value the USA leads (€82m) followed by the UK (€75m); volume and value rankings differ because price levels differ by market
slides.2.highlights.3.title: The supermarket price ladder
slides.2.highlights.3.content: 2025 average shelf prices in French supermarkets (excluding discounters, incl. VAT): Côtes du Rhône €3.93, Villages €5.43, Crozes-Hermitage €12.12, Gigondas €13.97; Ventoux €3.54, Luberon €4.18 (Inter Rhône)
slides.2.content: The brand role of Côtes du Rhône: a high-volume, low-price, highly visible entry wine that draws consumers into the Rhône ladder.
slides.3.title: Négociants and estates: illustrated with verified names
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Guigal
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Founded in 1946 by Étienne Guigal, who had worked 15 years at Vidal-Fleury; later bought Vidal-Fleury (1984) and Château d'Ampuis (1995) among others; known for the Côte-Rôtie 'La La' single vineyards (La Mouline, La Landonne, La Turque) (Wikipedia)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Paul Jaboulet Aîné
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Founded in 1834 by Antoine Jaboulet at Tain l'Hermitage; managed by Caroline Frey from 2006; its flagship is Hermitage La Chapelle (the house calls the 1961 one of the iconic wines of the 20th century) (official history page)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Other representative négociants
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Large northern Rhône houses such as Chapoutier and Delas are named only; founding dates and ownership were not individually verified for this lesson, so they are not stated or examined
slides.3.highlights.3.title: Independent estates and co-operatives
slides.3.highlights.3.content: Independent estates win on single sites, terroir and brand; co-operatives (87 in 2024/25) pool small growers for scale and steady supply. Together with traders they form the Rhône's three-way supply chain (Inter Rhône)
slides.3.content: In industry answers use the pattern 'founding year + positioning + flagship wine', and state only verified facts.
slides.4.title: Price pressure and industry responses
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Volume and stocks
slides.4.highlights.0.content: 2025 production was 2,012,313 hl, about 7% below 2024 (2,165,446 hl); at 1 August 2025 grower stocks were 2,263,241 hl (-7%) and trader stocks 783,920 hl (-1%) (Inter Rhône)
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Bulk prices
slides.4.highlights.1.content: The 2024-vintage red Côtes du Rhône averaged €133.30/hl over seven months (+9%) and white €191.30/hl (Réussir, 2 May 2025, data to end February 2025); southern crus rose in bulk sales while rosé despatches fell 12%
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Price benchmarks (2026–27)
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Vinetur reports Inter Rhône published non-binding economic benchmarks for 2026–27 red Côtes du Rhône: conventional and HVE €132 (equilibrium) / €171 (sustainability) per hl, organic €148 / €193; a negotiating reference, not a minimum price (secondary source, not examined)
slides.4.highlights.3.title: Rebalancing towards white and rosé
slides.4.highlights.3.content: 2025 output mix: red 73%, rosé 14%, white 13%. wein.plus reports a regional goal of white plus rosé reaching one third within ten years (the report is undated, so treat it as strategic direction; not examined)
slides.4.content: Essay skeleton: oversupply and shifting demand → price pressure → responses (rebalancing, price benchmarks, exports and premiumisation) → trade-offs.
slides.5.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge check
According to Inter Rhône's 2025 data, what are the top three export markets by volume, in order?
A. Belgium, UK, USA
B. USA, UK, Germany
C. China, Japan, USA
D. Germany, Netherlands, Canada
By volume: Belgium 18%, UK 17%, USA 13%; by value the USA is first.
In 2024/25, what was the largest despatch form from Rhône cellars?
A. Packaged (bottled)
B. Fresh grapes
C. Bulk
D. Barrel-aged spirits
Bulk was about 64%, packaged about 31% and fresh grapes about 5% (Inter Rhône, 2024/25).
What is Inter Rhône's role in the industry?
A. The brand of a single wine house
B. The government tax authority
C. An interprofession of growers and traders handling statistics, promotion and market coordination
D. A pure export company
Inter Rhône is the valley's interprofession; its Chiffres clés is the main data source of this lesson.
Which ranking (low to high) of 2025 French supermarket average shelf prices matches Inter Rhône's data?
A. Gigondas < Côtes du Rhône < Villages
B. Côtes du Rhône < Villages < Crozes-Hermitage < Gigondas
C. Villages < Côtes du Rhône < Gigondas
D. All the same price
€3.93 < €5.43 < €12.12 < €13.97 (2025, supermarkets excluding discounters). Exact amounts change yearly; the point is the ladder.
